questions.question: Who excavated Mohenjodaro in 1922?
questions.explanation:
R.D. Banerji is correct: he excavated Mohenjodaro in 1922.
Daya Ram Sahni is incorrect: he excavated Harappa in 1921.
S.R. Rao is incorrect: he is known for excavating Lothal after Independence.
B.B. Lal is incorrect: he is associated with later excavations such as Kalibangan.
So the answer is R.D. Banerji.

questions.question: Harappa is located on the banks of which river?
questions.explanation:
Ravi is correct: Harappa lies on the Ravi in Punjab (Pakistan).
Indus is incorrect: Mohenjodaro, not Harappa, is on the Indus.
Sutlej is incorrect: Ropar lies on the Sutlej.
Beas is incorrect: no major Harappan city is associated with the Beas.
So the answer is Ravi.

questions.question: Dholavira, a major Harappan city, is located in which state of India?
questions.explanation:
Gujarat is correct: Dholavira lies in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
Rajasthan is incorrect: Kalibangan is the well-known Harappan site there.
Haryana is incorrect: Rakhigarhi and Banawali are the well-known sites there.
Punjab is incorrect: Ropar is the well-known site in Indian Punjab.
So the answer is Gujarat.

questions.question: Evidence of a ploughed field has been found at which Harappan site?
questions.explanation:
Kalibangan is correct: a ploughed field with furrows was found at Kalibangan in Rajasthan.
Lothal is incorrect: it is known for its dockyard.
Mohenjodaro is incorrect: it is known for the Great Bath.
Harappa is incorrect: it is known for its granaries and cemeteries.
So the answer is Kalibangan.

questions.question: The stone statue known as the 'Priest-King' was found at:
questions.explanation:
Mohenjodaro is correct: the bearded 'Priest-King' bust was found at Mohenjodaro.
Harappa, Lothal and Kalibangan are incorrect: the statue does not come from these sites.
So the answer is Mohenjodaro.

questions.question: Why is the Indus Valley Civilisation also called the Harappan Civilisation?
options: Harappa was the first site of this civilisation to be discovered
Harappa is the only site with a citadel
Harappa is the only site with seals
questions.explanation:
Harappa was the first site of this civilisation to be discovered is correct: archaeologists name a culture after the site where it was first found.
Harappa was its capital city is incorrect: no capital of the civilisation has been identified.
Harappa is the only site with a citadel is incorrect: Mohenjodaro, Kalibangan and others also had citadels.
Harappa is the only site with seals is incorrect: seals are found at many sites.
So the answer is that Harappa was the first site discovered.

questions.question: The Harappans were among the earliest people in the world to grow which fibre crop?
questions.explanation:
Cotton is correct: the Harappans were among the earliest to grow cotton and weave cotton cloth.
Jute, Hemp and Flax are incorrect: these are not the fibre crops linked with the Harappans.
So the answer is Cotton.

questions.question: Who was the Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India when the discovery of the new civilisation was announced in 1924?
questions.explanation:
John Marshall is correct: as Director-General of the ASI, he announced the discovery of a new civilisation in 1924.
Alexander Cunningham is incorrect: he was the first Director-General of the ASI, in the 19th century.
Mortimer Wheeler is incorrect: he became Director-General in 1944.
James Prinsep is incorrect: he deciphered Brahmi and was never head of the ASI.
So the answer is John Marshall.

questions.question: Which were the main food grains of the Harappans?
questions.explanation:
Wheat and barley is correct: these were the main grains grown in the Harappan region.
Rice and maize and Ragi and maize are incorrect: maize came to India only from the Americas, thousands of years later.
Rice and sugarcane is incorrect: rice grains are rare at Harappan sites and sugarcane is not a food grain.
So the answer is wheat and barley.

questions.question: The many terracotta female figurines found at Harappan sites are generally believed to represent:
questions.explanation:
A mother goddess is correct: many scholars see these figurines as linked with the worship of a mother goddess (fertility cult).
Queens of Harappa is incorrect: there is no evidence of named queens or royal portraits.
The Vedic goddess Usha is incorrect: the Vedas were composed later.
Buddhist goddesses is incorrect: Buddhism arose much later.
So the answer is a mother goddess.
